problems.title: Cluster-density definitions and reported values disagree
problems.source_claim: PCD/NCD count disjoint positive/negative co-clusters divided by a common total sequence count; repeated tables represent the same encoder comparison.
locations: PDF p6 Table3 vs p29 Table7
assumptions: Every counted cluster contains a generated sequence and clusters are disjoint.
The written denominator is common total generated or generated-plus-reference sequences.
Three-decimal table rounding bounded by 0.0005 per entry.
problems.check: P+N <= G <= M implies PCD+NCD <=1. Dataset .990+.304=1.294; flow .214+.945=1.159, with minimum rounded sums1.293/1.158. ESMcCD .963 vs .863 differs .100. RFDiffusion USR prose .06 vs table .07.
problems.result: Printed definitions and values cannot all be correct as written; replacement values unresolved.
problems.counterevidence: Different conditional denominators could produce sums above1 but require corrected definitions. Either ESMc number remains below ESM2-650M .986; either RFD USR remains below DiMA .10. Other primary metric comparisons are not refuted.
problems.impact: Local metric interpretation/reporting defect, not a demonstrated reversal of central comparative conclusions.

correction.detail: Recover authoritative cluster denominators/counts and run-specific values; no invented replacement.

problems.title: pLDDT averaging drops within-rank sequence multiplicity
problems.source_claim: pLDDT evaluated over generated samples; released helper calculates each prediction then returns sequence-keyed dictionary.
assumptions: Duplicate strings occur within a rank and not all unique sequence scores are equal.
Counterexample uses deterministic admissible scores90 and30; no actual folding-model values are asserted.
problems.check: A,A,A,B with q(A)=90,q(B)=30 gives draw mean75, one-rank unique mean60. Equal shards[A,A],[A,B] give averaged localunique means75, demonstrating partition dependence even when shard sizes equal.
problems.result: Source computes distinct-sequence mean per rank, not ordinary generated-draw mean.
problems.counterevidence: Unique-output quality is defensible if declared; no duplicates/equal scores remove discrepancy. No historical source binding, generated multiplicities or score shifts are available.
problems.impact: Released-evaluator semantics correction; historical central quality/ranking effect Needs Evidence.

correction.detail: Retain sample-index scores or cache by sequence then use occurrence-weighted sums/counts across ranks.

problems.title: Decoder training denormalizes twice
problems.source_claim: The decoder is a core DiMA component; advertised token reconstruction fine-tunes it for decoding generated normalized embeddings through the same inverse-normalization interface.
locations: PDF p2 Figure1, p3 Token Reconstruction, p26 Table5
assumptions: Default ESM2/transformer decoder configuration and documented Stage 2 training route with normalizer enabled.
Stored mean mu and positive std s>=1e-5; for nonidentity statistics D(D(z)) differs generically from D(z).
Finite interface counterexample is admissible algebra, not actual ESM embeddings, a measured learned decoder, or a recovered historical experiment.
problems.check: D(z)=s z+mu; training D(D(z)), generation D(z), difference s(s-1)z+s mu. Equal raw encodings-1,3 have mean1,std2 and normalized-1,+1: training inputs-1,7, inference-1,3. Logits(0,u-5) separate training labels but fail second inference label.
problems.result: A core learned decoder is trained and validated on D(D(z)) but deployed on D(z); the valid finite example proves that fitting/validation success does not generally transfer through the mismatched interface.
problems.counterevidence: Identity statistics, fixed-point inputs or decoder invariance can remove the discrepancy. README permits skipping Stage 2 using pretrained lm_head; other encoders and historically different code are outside the demonstrated dependency. Actual normalization tensors/checkpoints and historical bindings are missing, so quantitative score losses remain unknown.
problems.impact: Major for the pinned default ESM2/transformer learned-decoder route under nonidentity normalization: the advertised core component's training/validation contract is inconsistent with generation. This does not require a measured benchmark loss or whole-model collapse. Historical finetuning gains, magnitude of score effects and other configurations remain Needs Evidence.

correction.detail: Remove outer denormalization in loss_step, retain batch_get_logits inverse once. This restores a common single-map input contract but does not validate checkpoints or benchmark performance.

problems.core_dependency: Paper Figure1/Token Reconstruction/Table5 -> config selects ESM2+transformer -> transformer and output projection are newly constructed -> README Stage2 trains and validates via loss_step/batch_get_logits with two inverse maps -> base_trainer.pred_logits uses batch_decode with one inverse map. Parent independently read each cited source segment during focused post-batch acceptance.

acceptance_correction.reason: Established default core dependency and invalid training/validation-to-generation interface; unknown historical benchmark effect is retained as a scope limitation rather than a requirement for Major.

problems.title: CHEAP shorten-two mask reduces requested length twice
problems.source_claim: Shorten-two latent representation compresses sequence length by two and generation samples requested raw lengths.
assumptions: Length sampler returns raw sequence length; output slice is governed by2*mask.sum.
problems.check: Latent widthceil254/2=127; active countceil(min254,127)/2=64; output length capped128 rather than254. Parent independently evaluates integer arithmetic.
problems.result: Generic optional-path length interface error proved without any external CHEAP execution.
problems.counterevidence: Current configured/pretrained path is shorten1; original shorten2 experiment binding is absent.
problems.impact: Minor optional-release defect; no historical Table3/11 effect established.

correction.detail: Clamp each raw length to raw maximum then compress once, m_i=ceil(min(l_i,Lmax)/2), bounded by latentwidth; retain original rawlength for exact odd-length output trimming.
